documents.title: Lamar University Guidance on the Use of Generative AI
tiers: Prohibition of generative AI tool use
Allowed in specified contexts with attribution
Encouragement of generative AI tool use
documents.summary: University-wide guidance naming Microsoft Copilot as the approved platform, a four-tier data classification limiting what may be entered into AI tools, and prohibited uses (including no AI grading and no uploading student work). It leaves course rules to instructors with three sample syllabus tiers, and adds research guidance on authorship, disclosure and peer review.
documents.stance_why: The guidance sets data and platform rules for everyone but leaves classroom AI use to instructors: "Instructors have discretion over whether and how generative AI tools fit their course's learning outcomes", and it supplies three sample syllabus statements (prohibition, allowed with attribution, encouragement) as "a starting point", so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: States the institution's stance: "supports responsible exploration of generative AI tools"; a framework principle for all users, so P56, and it welcomes use (encourage).
units.anchor: Lamar University supports responsible exploration of generative AI tools.

units.why: Defines generative AI ("a form of artificial intelligence trained on large datasets"), which sets what the guidance covers, so P61.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a form of artificial intelligence trained on large datasets

units.why: A general principle ("should remain mindful of") listing the concerns that frame the whole guidance; a preamble principle so P56 rather than any one specific rule.
units.anchor: Users should remain mindful of information security, data privacy, compliance standards, copyright

units.why: Scope statement: "the formal policy governs" over this guidance, an institution-level framework relation, so P56.
units.anchor: Where this document and the formal policy differ, the formal policy governs.

units.why: Names a licensed, university-reviewed assistant: "approved generative AI platform". P17 (sanctioned tool) fits better than P50 because it designates the tool rather than stating a data rule.
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot is Lamar University's approved generative AI platform

units.why: Warns that the Copilot privacy banner does not allow entering anything: "does not mean any information may be entered freely"; a data-protection limit, P50.
units.anchor: This does not mean any information may be entered freely.

units.why: "must be critically evaluated before use" requires users to verify AI output, matching P31.
units.anchor: Generated content must be critically evaluated before use.

units.why: Assigns responsibility to the person: "not the university, is responsible for that content". Ownership of what one publishes, P29.
units.anchor: The individual publishing AI-assisted content, not the university, is responsible for that content.

documents.title: Guidance: Syllabus Policies on AI Usage
documents.summary: A 2025 CITL blog post of sample syllabus language in three categories, with reasons to include an AI statement and a set of external examples. The Lamar samples cover prohibited use, permitted use with restrictions and cited output, and encouraged use of Copilot with attribution.
documents.stance_why: The post says "AI policies can broadly be divided into three categories; Prohibited, Permitted with Restrictions, or Encouraged" and offers sample statements for instructors to adopt or adapt, so it hands the choice to instructors with tiers.

notes: No school-level or computing-unit AI policy found; course layer deferred in the collect file. The CST-hosted PDF is a revised version of the CTLE PDF (same origin); both coded in full as instructed. Uncovered units: AI-enabled phishing/deepfake security awareness (in both guidance docs) and instructors discussing AI ethics with students (coded once per document). The CTLE guideline 2 template contradicts itself (allows AI with attribution, then bars submitting AI-generated text); both coded. The external university examples in the CITL post are not Lamar policy and were not coded. Page-navigation text in the CITL file was ignored.
